title: Edge Environment Ops — Weeknotes & Blocker Triage (Mar 15-19 2027)
body:
Purpose:
A concise capture of the weeks field engineering notes related to edge / private deployments (VPC and on-prem). Focus: hard blockers seen across three customer installs, telemetry gaps that hinder debugging, and quick tactical mitigations for next week. Notes are intentionally informalsprint/ops-first.
summary: Overall week: mixed. Two installs finished functional validation, one customer (Acadia) still blocked by network path MTU and intermittent KMS timeouts. Telemetry gaps slowed triage for ~9 hours across two incidents. Actionable mitigations identified and owners assigned.
highlights:
- Acadia: full node provisioning succeeded; app containers crash when NGINX fronting tries to route to local sidecar (probable MTU/path fragmentation).
- Zenith: Canary rollout (quant-8 variant) passed 50k token smoke tests; latency within SLA after kernel patch.
- Kappa: onprem airgap install completed hardware walk; final KMS integration pending HSM cert exchange.
meeting_attendees: Marcus Chen (owner), Leah Gomez (field eng), Priya Raman (infra), Owen Blake (network), Zeynep Kaya (SRE oncall), Maya Singh (solutions eng), Customer PMs: Acadia - Tom Ruiz, Kappa - Hannah Lee
customer_blockers:
1) Acadia (PD-5192): Symptom: repeated 502s during high-throughput tokenization (~>1.2k r/s). Root candidates: path MTU causing TCP fragmentation between customer LB and node sidecar; observed PMTU blackholes on traceroute during load. Temp mitigation: enable MSS clamping on LB (customer infra) and lower instance egress mtu to 1400 (field patch). Owner: Owen Blake. ETA for verification: 2027-03-21.

2) Kappa (PD-5237): Symptom: KMS handshake times out intermittently during startup (~30-45s), causing service to fall into degraded mode until manual restart. Root cause likely HSM certificate chain ordering and CRL fetchs blocked by proxy rules. Proposed fix: push rotation script that retries handshake with exponential backoff + cached cert bundle; work with Kappa security to open CRL endpoints. Owner: Priya Raman + Kappa infra lead. ETA: 2027-03-23.

3) Acadia (follow-up): audit-log ingestion missing tracer attributes; we saw only 60% of expected KV cache hit metrics. Impact: slower duplicate-request debugging. Short-term: turn on DEBUG-level agent logs for 12h and stream to secure bucket. Long-term: add heartbeat/sequence id to cache events (infra ticket NET-245). Owner: Leah Gomez. ETA: 2027-03-18.
observations_and_root_causes:
- Network: two customers on older LB firmware with buggy PMTU discovery; bi-directional fragmentation not detected. We should add a PMTU probe during preflight to catch this class of failure.
- Runtime: observed a kernel OOO scheduling spike on 2 of 8 GPUS on Zenith during quant runs; backported patch from release-engineering reduced tail latency. Reference PR: runtime#1284.
- Security/KMS: cert chain validation in the agent assumes CRL reachable; in air-gapped installs we need a fallthrough cache for last-known-good CRLs.
- Telemetry: current platform agent drops KV cache trace when buffer > 256KB; large prompt prefixes triggered the drop and obscured correlation IDs.
decisions_made:
- Add PMTU handshake to preflight checklist and fail fast with explicit remediation instructions. (Decision by Marcus + Owen)
- Temporarily increase agent log retention for customer-facing debug sessions (consent documented) and rotate logs within 48h. (Decision by Leah + Priya)
- For air-gapped KMS installs, accept cached CRL approach as interim; design HSM cert exchange flow for secure transfer in next sprint. (Decision by Security + Solutions Eng)
action_items:
- Owen: MSS clamping config and verification with Acadia infra; follow up call Thurs 3/18. (PD-5192)
- Priya: implement exponential backoff + retry wrapper for KMS handshake; test against Kappa HSM simulator. (KMS-74)
- Leah: enable DEBUG agent logs on Acadia for 12h window and push to diagnostic bucket; redact secrets.
- Marcus: add PMTU probe to preflight script and create PR for templates; target branch: deploy-playbooks.
- Maya: prepare customer-facing writeup summarizing root cause and mitigation steps for Acadia and Kappa (to be shared by 3/20).
- Zeynep: add SLO alert rule to detect >30s repeated KMS handshake failures and page SRE oncall.

All owners: update linked Jira tickets with notes and attach packet captures where available.
risks_and_escorts:
- If MSS clamping is refused by a customer firewall team, we need an edge NAT-based workaround; estimate +2–3 days.
- Airgap KMS fixes may require on-site HSM access, adding travel and scheduling risk.
- Missing telemetry can delay ramp of other installs; prioritize NET-245 in next sprint planning.
next_week_plan:
- Run preflight PMTU probes on next three scheduled installs and collect results in central spreadsheet.
- Ship temporary agent debug toggle and document safe use.
- Continue KMS handshake retry work and perform integration test with Kappa this week.
- SRE/Field sync Wed 10:30am PT: focus on escalations and paging noise.
- Post-mortem (if Acadia persists past 3/21) to capture lessons learned and update onboarding runbook.
appendix:
Useful links and quick notes:
- Packet captures saved: gs://private-deploy-diagnostics/acadia-2027-03-16/pcap1.gz
- Preflight probe script location: github.com/redwood-inference/deploy-playbooks/tree/pmtu-probe
- Relevant Jira: PD-5192, NET-231, KMS-74, NET-245
- Quick commands to reproduce environment: (local) ./scripts/run-node.sh --env=acadia-staging --mtu=1400

A couple of loose thoughts:
- Consider adding a low-friction observable: a small ephemeral tracer that emits a one-line PMTU/MTU check from customer LB to node; no persistent logs, just a response code to the console. Could reduce TTFD on network issues.
- We should add a checkbox in the Console UI for "air-gapped KMS mode" that toggles cert caching and hides CRL fetch attempts in agent logs to reduce noise for customers who expect offline operation.
notes_meta: Informal capture for field team; please copy into Confluence page for finalized runbook updates. If anything is missing or misattributed, ping Marcus.
file_notes: Draft uploaded to drive for review 2027-03-19. Intend to close action items and move final summary to confluence by 2027-03-22.
